title: Interpretability: coefficients, feature importance, SHAP and partial dependence

videos.script: A caller from the retention team asks one question. Why this subscriber? {{why}} A manager asks another. What drives churn? {{drives}} A logistic regression answers with its weights, if you read the categories against each other. {{weights}} A forest's own importance ranks a column of pure noise second. Shuffling the columns on the test months puts it last. {{noise}} Partial dependence finds lesson fourteen's cliffs inside the boosted trees. {{pdp}} SHAP shares out one prediction among the columns, and the shares add up exactly. {{shap}} Then the monthly plan, and an explanation that turns out to be about the encoder, not the customers. {{monthly}} By the end, you can explain a model, and you know what an explanation does not say. {{end}}
